facts.text: Cold Spring was named for the many springs near its original site and was first home to Ojibwe, Winnebago, and Dakota peoples.
The CSBC beverage company, founded in 1874 by German immigrant Michael Sargl, still produces soft drinks, beer, and energy drinks.
Cold Spring boasts three National Register of Historic Places sites: the 1907 John Oster House, Ferdinand Peters House, and the 1912 Eugene Hermanutz House.
The town sits at the gateway of the Sauk River Chain of Lakes, a connected system of 14 bay‑like lakes fed by the Sauk River.
During the grasshopper plagues of the 1870s, residents built Assumption Chapel—also called the Grasshopper Chapel—to seek relief from the locusts.
German‑speaking Catholics were drawn to the area by missionary Francis Xavier Pierz, who advertised in German newspapers and promised a land flowing with milk and honey.
